source_title: Ford Ranger 3.2TDCi XLT 4X4 A/T P/U D/C -- Autonet Helderberg specification sheet (Gross Laden Mass 3200 kg; Licencing/Tare Mass 2118 kg)
notes: GVM (Gross Laden Mass) is 3200 kg for the South African-market Ranger T6 3.2 TDCi XLT 4x4 double cab. This exact page is for the 6-speed automatic derivative (tare 2118 kg), not the manual derivative this row's existing curb_mass_kg (2159 kg, confirmed separately via carfolio.com for the manual 3.2 TDCi XLT 4x4) describes. GVM on this platform is an axle/chassis rating set by the frame and suspension, not the transmission or engine -- confirmed independently by a second, unrelated listing for the 2.0 SiT XLT 4x4 double cab (a different engine and a lower tare of 2044 kg) that states the identical 3200 kg GVM, so the rating is not engine- or trim-specific. Implied payload against the row's existing curb mass: 3200 - 2159 = 1041 kg, plausible for a 4x4 double-cab bakkie.

source_title: RDW (Netherlands national vehicle register) open data, dataset m9d7-ebf2 "Gekentekende voertuigen": BMW 530E, variant 11AG, massa ledig voertuig 1810 kg, technisch toelaatbare maximummassa 2505 kg
notes: RDW is the Dutch national registration/type-approval database; technische_max_massa_voertuig is the EU technically permissible maximum laden mass. 894 registrations carry massa_ledig_voertuig=1810 and all state 2505 kg, all under one type-approval variant (11AG = 530e rear-drive, G30 LCI). The row's curb_mass_kg (1810 kg) matches RDW massa ledig voertuig exactly, so the pair is on one basis. Excludes 530e xDrive (RDW variant 31CG, leeg 1935 / max 2610). source_title: RDW (Netherlands national vehicle register) open data, dataset m9d7-ebf2 "Gekentekende voertuigen": MERCEDES-BENZ E 200, sedan, 1991 cc, variant U08KT0, massa ledig voertuig 1600 kg, technisch toelaatbare maximummassa 2360 kg
notes: Exact-variant confirmation: filtering handelsbenaming to exactly 'E 200' at massa_ledig_voertuig = 1600 kg (the row's own curb mass) returns 336 registrations, ALL under the single type-approval variant U08KT0, ALL 1991 cc sedans, and ALL stating technische_max_massa_voertuig = 2360 kg across eleven different uitvoering (equipment) codes -- so the permissible mass is a type-approval constant here, not equipment-dependent. Independently confirmed by automoli.com's W213-facelift-2020 technical-data table for the E 200 (197 PS) EQ Boost 9G-TRONIC: Leergewicht 1625 kg, zulaessiges Gesamtgewicht 2360 kg, Zuladung 735 kg (https://www.automoli.com/de/vehicles/mercedes-benz/klasa-e/klasa-e-w213-facelift-2020-7586/). Payload note: 2360 - 1600 = 760 kg, above the 350-700 kg rule of thumb for a passenger car. This is genuine and not a wrong figure -- the W213 executive saloon really does carry a ~735 kg rated Zuladung, and the extra 25 kg is the gap between this row's curb basis (1600 kg, matching RDW's driver-excluded massa ledig voertuig) and automoli's 1625 kg Leergewicht. Two independent sources state 2360 kg for this exact engine/body.

source_title: angurten.de technical-data table -- Ford Puma 1.0 l EcoBoost MHEV (125 PS), 92 kW, 999 cc, 6-speed manual, from 06/2020: Leergewicht 1280 kg, zul. Gesamtgewicht 1760 kg, Zuladung 480 kg
notes: Exact engine match: 999 cc, 92 kW (125 PS) mild-hybrid Puma, manual gearbox. The basis lines up exactly: the published Leergewicht of 1280 kg is this row's curb mass (1205 kg) plus the 75 kg driver that the EU kerb-weight definition includes, so 1205 kg is the driver-excluded figure and 1760 kg the type-approval permissible maximum for the same car. Confirmed independently by RDW (Netherlands national register, dataset m9d7-ebf2): at merk FORD, handelsbenaming PUMA, massa_ledig_voertuig = 1205 kg, type-approval variant B7JB12X states technische_max_massa_voertuig = 1760 kg on 17 of 18 registrations. RDW also shows 1760 kg recurring at unladen masses 1180, 1215 and 1219 kg, i.e. across equipment levels, which is why the same figure is applied to both the ST-Line and Titanium X rows -- while the heavier Puma type approvals (1785 kg at unladen 1201-1226, 1830/1835 kg at unladen 1234-1279) are deliberately excluded as different powertrains/gearboxes. Implied useful load 1760 - 1205 = 555 kg (= the maker's stated 480 kg Zuladung plus the 75 kg driver), inside the 350-700 kg band.

source_title: RDW (Netherlands national vehicle register) open data, dataset m9d7-ebf2 "Gekentekende voertuigen": SKODA OCTAVIA, 1498 cc, 5 seats, variant ACDHFAX0, uitvoering NFD7FD7CW0054BIVL0C1ASA, massa ledig voertuig 1338 kg, technisch toelaatbare maximummassa 1888 kg
notes: At massa_ledig_voertuig = 1338 kg (this row's exact curb mass) the register holds 13 Octavias, all 1498 cc, all 5-seat, all under the single type-approval variant ACDHFAX0 and the single uitvoering code NFD7FD7CW0054BIVL0C1ASA, all stating 1888 kg. The one other hit at that unladen mass is a 1984 cc car from 2019 with no variant recorded and is excluded. Cross-checked against Skoda's own technical-data sheet for the fourth-generation (NX) Octavia, engine column '1.5 TSI/110 kW' (the row's 110 kW / 1498 cc manual): kerb weight incl. 75 kg driver 1353-1511 kg, payload 474-609 kg, total weight 1850-1910 kg (https://cdn.skoda-storyboard.com/2024/05/Octavia_technical_data_EN_842ba18d.pdf). 1888 kg sits inside that published total-weight range and 1338 + 75 = 1413 kg inside the published kerb range, so the register figure is consistent with the manufacturer for this exact engine. Caveat recorded deliberately: Skoda publishes the total weight as a RANGE (1850-1910 kg) because it varies with body and equipment, so 1888 kg is not a single type-approval constant for '1.5 TSI 110 kW' in general -- it is the figure the register attaches to precisely the equipment whose unladen mass equals this row's curb mass, which is what makes the pair self-consistent. The registrations carrying it are 2022 first-admissions of the same NX generation as this 2020 row. Implied useful load 550 kg, inside the 350-700 kg band.
